The image is a microscopic view (100 µm scale bar) showing:

- Branching conidiophores (elongated stalks)
- Dense clusters of round, globular conidia arranged in grape-like masses at the tips
- Hyaline to lightly pigmented, spherical spores in botryose clusters

This morphology is highly diagnostic of **Botrytis cinerea** — the causal agent of Gray Mold. The branching conidiophores bearing clusters of round conidia are the textbook microscopic signature of this pathogen. The symptom description confirms: "spores are light brown-gray on black stalks" and "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass."

No other class in the list produces this clustered, grape-like conidial arrangement at this scale.
